Use `StaticFiles` and mount it on a path. You can serve static files automatically from a directory using `StaticFiles`.[1]

The steps are:
- Import `StaticFiles`.[1]
- "Mount" a `StaticFiles()` instance in a specific path.[1]

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

app = FastAPI()

app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")
```

**What the parameters mean:**
- The first `"/static"` refers to the sub-path this "sub-application" will be "mounted" on. So, any path that starts with `"/static"` will be handled by it.[3]
- The `directory="static"` refers to the name of the directory that contains your static files.[3]
- The `name="static"` gives it a name that can be used internally by **FastAPI**.[3]

All these parameters can be different than "`static`", adjust them to the needs and specific details of your own application.[3]

For example, with a CSS file at `static/styles.css`, because you are using `StaticFiles`, that CSS file would be served automatically by your **FastAPI** application at the URL `/static/styles.css`.[5]

**Tip:** If you need to host a frontend, use `app.frontend()` instead[1]. `app.frontend()` uses `StaticFiles` underneath, with several additional advantages for frontends, like handling client-side routing.[1]

More info: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/static-files/
